title: A Asset for the Protocol
premise: Sable Yarrow, a veteran crash investigator, has spent nine years burying the truth about Flight 4471—the flight that killed her family in row twelve and was quietly erased from every database. When a live transatlantic flight vanishes mid-air from all records while she watches it happen on her own tracking rig, Sable realizes the same protocol that erased her family's tragedy is still running, and that her old cover identity is its next target. Armed with a corrupted black box recovered by a guilt-ridden insider, she races across three countries to deliver evidence of a state-sponsored disposal program to an international tribunal, hunted by an assassin who once spared her and now cannot again. In the end, Sable chooses to testify under her real name—trading her invisibility for belonging—and burns the protocol's archive to ash, though the cost is the last person who ever felt like home.
about_author: Lena Blackwood is a former aviation insurance analyst who spent a decade reading accident reports most people never see. She writes thrillers about the paper trails behind disasters, and lives off-grid with two dogs and a shortwave radio.

chapters.title: Row Twelve
chapters.summary: Sable Yarrow's POV. On the ninth anniversary of the crash that killed her parents and sister, Sable works a routine runway incident by day and drinks alone by night, her go-bag packed by the door. A flashback reveals the polished lie: she changed her name after the investigation into Flight 4471 was shut down. Emotional beat: grief worn as routine, and the first crack in it.

chapters.title: The Ghost at 37,000 Feet
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Running her private ADS-B rig for solace, Sable watches Flight 2219 vanish from every tracker, every database, mid-flight over the Atlantic—no mayday, no wreckage report, nothing. Her calls to colleagues are met with confusion: no such flight number exists. Emotional beat: vertigo—the past reaching into the present, and the sick recognition of a signature she knows.

chapters.title: What the Protocol Keeps
chapters.summary: Alternating POV introduces Marcus Vane, the assassin contracted by 'the Protocol,' a covert tri-government program that makes inconvenient aircraft disappear. Vane reviews his next file—and finds Sable's real name flagged for termination. Meanwhile Sable digs up her old case notes. Emotional beat: cold institutional menace versus hot personal dread converging on one woman.

chapters.title: The Man Who Missed
chapters.summary: Vane breaks into Sable's apartment to stage an accident but finds her go-bag gone; she'd left hours earlier after spotting surveillance. Their near-encounter ends with him letting her slip away—an echo of a mercy he showed once before. Sable flees to Reykjavik, following a lead to a retired air traffic controller. Emotional beat: hunter and prey circling, both haunted.

chapters.title: Black Box, Broken Chain
chapters.summary: In Reykjavik, whistleblower Edda Halldors, a former Protocol technician drowning in guilt, gives Sable a corrupted black box from Flight 4471—proof the erasure program predates her family's crash. Before they can decrypt it, Protocol operatives hit the safehouse; Edda stays behind so Sable can run. Emotional beat: the burden of inheritance—truth passed like a debt.

chapters.title: Three Governments, One Door
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Denied asylum in Iceland and tipped off that British intelligence wants her 'contained,' Sable realizes no state will help her—each is compromised. She contacts journalist Theo Brandt, her sister's old friend, the one thread of trust she has left. Emotional beat: isolation sharpening into resolve; belonging reduced to a single fragile alliance.

chapters.title: Everything Vane Was
chapters.summary: Vane's POV. Ordered to finish the job publicly this time, Vane traces Sable through Brandt and confronts her in Hamburg—but the decrypted black box data names Vane's own brother among Flight 4471's erased crew. Shaken, he gives Sable forty-eight hours instead of a bullet. Emotional beat: the assassin discovering he, too, was always an asset.

chapters.title: Forty-Eight Hours
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Sable and Brandt race to assemble testimony for a tribunal hearing in The Hague while Protocol scrambles to discredit them, framing Sable for the Reykjavik safehouse fire. Vane feeds them access codes, knowing it signs his death warrant. Emotional beat: desperate momentum, alliances forged under fire, the clock bleeding out.

chapters.title: The Hearing
chapters.summary: Climax. At the tribunal, Protocol's lawyers produce doctored records painting Sable as delusional—until Vane walks in with the original master archive key and testifies to the program himself. Gunfire erupts as Protocol's enforcers attempt a final silencing; Brandt takes a bullet meant for Sable and dies in her arms. Emotional beat: truth spoken at maximum cost.

chapters.title: Sable, Unhidden
chapters.summary: Resolution. Weeks later, the Protocol is exposed, its archive burned, investigations opened in three capitals. Sable buries Brandt beside her family and unpacks the go-bag for the first time in nine years, keeping only row twelve's photograph. She signs her real name to the public record. Emotional beat: inheritance reclaimed—grief transformed into belonging, visibility chosen at last.
